claimed.text: Nuccetelli testified to incursions near Vandenberg in 2003 to 2005 during NRO launches, objects he likened to flying buildings, each witnessed by multiple personnel and reported up the chain; he said official Air Force records of it are now held by AARO and the FBI, and that one witness was threatened and told to keep quiet.

Wiggins testified that on 15 February 2023 USS Jackson recorded four self-luminous Tic-Tac-shaped objects on its Star SAFIRE system, one emerging from the ocean, departing with near-instantaneous acceleration. The video was later published by Jeremy Corbell and by Knapp, who testified at the same hearing.

Knapp testified that documents paint a different picture from what the public and Congress have been told and that UAP material has been moved to private contractors; asked for names, he named Lockheed, a Dr. James Ryder at Lockheed and Glenn Gaffney of the CIA, and offered Burchett a list. The sourcing behind the names has not been published and no committee has reported receiving the list.

Knapp said he had confirmed on the record that Robert Bigelow and a colleague negotiated with Lockheed Martin executives to receive unusual material held in California, material he said was not made here.
Knapp told the Task Force that acts against witnesses are carried out by persons unknown, as Grusch, in the room, knew, including events in recent days; no member asked what he meant.

Borland testified that after a 2012 sighting at Langley his career was deliberately obstructed for more than a decade, that he filed complaints with AARO in March 2023 and the Intelligence Community Inspector General in August 2023, and that suppression of witnesses had probably been extremely widespread. He later said on American Alchemy that AARO transmitted an uncorrected memorandum of his interview.
Mace said at the hearing that they leaked Grusch's private medical information, and Moskowitz said he did not know what was true but knew members were being lied to.
Burlison played footage he described as an MQ-9 firing a Hellfire missile at an orb off Yemen in October 2024.

NewsNation reported that the Pentagon missed Luna's video deadline in April 2026 and that she publicly raised a subpoena; in May 2026 she said prior AARO leadership had been set up to block information and that Kosloski had apologised to members of Congress.

contested.text: The board infers that no subpoena had issued by August 2026, either after Luna's missed deadline or across the committee's three UAP hearings.
The board infers that no House UAP hearing was held between 9 September 2025 and August 2026, a period of executive releases and floor action without contemporaneous testimony.
AARO's own video channel before PURSUE was seven short clips released over five weeks, one resolved as birds; the board reads their timing after the September testimony as minimum compliance.
The names Knapp gave under oath rest on sourcing that has not been published, which is why the board grades them as testimony rather than record.

lead.text: The House Oversight Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, chaired by Anna Paulina Luna, held the third House UAP hearing on 9 September 2025, with witnesses Jeffrey Nuccetelli, Alexandro Wiggins, George Knapp, Dylan Borland and, for the minority, Joe Spielberger of the Project On Government Oversight.

questions: What were the events in recent days against Grusch that Knapp referred to from the witness table?
Did the Defense Department ever answer Crane's July 2025 letter on the Grusch reprisal?
Does AARO hold the Vandenberg records Nuccetelli says it holds, and was the USS Jackson recording ever entered in AARO's case system?
Has Knapp's list of corporations reached any committee, and how does his past consultancy to BAASS bear on his account of the Lockheed transfer?
Has the Task Force obtained the witness list Grusch offered Mace in July 2023?

record.text: The roster printed in the hearing record gives Luna as chairwoman and Jasmine Crockett as ranking member, with Mace, Burchett, Boebert, Burlison, Crane and Gill on the majority side.

The hearing, Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection, met at 10:05 am in HVC-210 and was printed as Serial No. 119-44; Biggs, Begich, Ogles, Titus and Moskowitz were waived on to question witnesses, and Grothman was also present.

Luna's opening statement records that the Department of Defense told committee staff that only House Armed Services and Defense Appropriations members could be read in on the relevant special access programmes, and that any other member needs the approval of the chairman and ranking member of both.
In the same statement Luna called former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick a documented liar and warned against oversight bodies that become graveyards for testimony.

Rep. Eli Crane entered his 24 July 2025 letter to the Defense Department on reprisal against Grusch, citing removal of his clearance, denial of promotion and loss of medical retirement, and said he was still waiting for a reply. Grusch attended but did not testify.

Crockett, the ranking member, spoke of a long-standing overclassification problem and called Spielberger as the minority witness, devoting her round to the protections available to those who come forward.

Burlison told Wiggins from the dais that he was the first currently serving witness to come forward, and asked Borland whether BAASS was involved in reverse engineering of non-human intelligence craft.
At the hearing Burlison said his NDAA disclosure amendment had been ruled non-germane by staff and that House administration staff had blocked a full AARO briefing in 2024.

The majority's wrap-up release for the hearing said that agencies withheld information about UAP programmes, that witnesses face retaliation, that UAP spending flows to private entities outside FOIA's reach, and that personnel lack standard reporting protocols.
Burchett's H.R. 5060, the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act, was introduced on 29 August 2025 with Luna and Crane as cosponsors.

On 1 April 2026 Luna wrote to Hegseth for UAP video files after whistleblowers told the Task Force that AARO held more video records, saying UAP around military installations threaten the armed forces; the Department did not produce by the deadline.
The Task Force's 30 June 2026 hearing, on the CIA's MKULTRA project, heard Stephen Kinzer, Tom O'Neill and Elizabeth Ginexi; no UAP witness appeared.
Neither the Oversight Committee nor Luna holds any entitlement under 10 U.S.C. 119 to notice of waived special access programmes.

summary.text: Chairman James Comer announced the Task Force on 11 February 2025 and named Luna to chair it, and the two wrote to Secretary of State Rubio, Secretary of Defense Hegseth and CIA Director Ratcliffe asking for a briefing on all UAP records in their possession.

The September 2025 hearing put first-hand service witnesses and a journalist before the Task Force, and its record carries the Department's rule limiting special access programme read-ins and a letter about reprisal against David Grusch.

After testimony that AARO held more video, Luna wrote to Hegseth in April 2026 demanding it; the Task Force also hosted the June 2026 Capitol press conference, and its 30 June 2026 hearing was about MKULTRA, not UAP.
